questions.question_text: With which country does India conduct the bilateral naval exercise 'Varuna'?
questions.explanation: 'Varuna' is a bilateral Navy exercise conducted with France.
questions.subject: Defence

questions.question_text: The bilateral naval exercise 'Naseem Al Bahr' is held between India and...
questions.explanation: 'Naseem Al Bahr' is the bilateral Navy exercise conducted with Oman.
questions.subject: Defence

questions.question_text: Political right does NOT include which of the following?
questions.option_d: Right to lodge complaint with executive bodies of the Government
questions.explanation: Right to life is a civil/fundamental right (Article 21), whereas rights to vote, contest elections, and petition the government are political rights.
questions.subject: Indian Polity

questions.question_text: Freedom of the Press in India is-
questions.option_a: available to the people under the law of the Parliament
questions.option_c: implied in the right of freedom of expression
questions.option_d: available to the people of India under executive power
questions.explanation: Freedom of the Press is not explicitly mentioned but is implicit in the 'freedom of speech and expression' under Article 19(1)(a).
questions.subject: Indian Polity

questions.question_text: Who conducts the State Assembly Elections?
questions.explanation: The Election Commission of India conducts elections to Parliament and State Legislatures. State Election Commissions conduct local body elections.
questions.subject: Indian Polity

questions.question_text: Guru Shikhar is the highest point of which mountain range?
questions.explanation: Located in Rajasthan, Guru Shikhar at 1,722 meters is the highest peak of the Aravalli Range.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.question_text: Which of these rivers does NOT drain into the Bay of Bengal?
questions.explanation: The Narmada is a west-flowing river that drains into the Arabian Sea.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.question_text: Which of the following blood groups is known as the 'universal recipient'?
questions.explanation: People with blood group AB (specifically AB-positive) are called universal recipients because they can receive blood from any blood group, as they have no antibodies against A, B, or Rh antigens.
questions.subject: General Science

questions.question_text: Which element is found in all organic compounds?
questions.explanation: Organic chemistry is the study of carbon-containing compounds. Carbon's ability to form strong bonds with itself and other elements makes it the backbone of organic molecules.
questions.subject: General Science

questions.question_text: Who was the first Governor General of Bengal?
questions.explanation: Warren Hastings became the first Governor-General of Bengal in 1773 under the Regulating Act of 1773.
questions.subject: Modern India

questions.question_text: During the Mughal period which one of the following traders first came to India?
questions.explanation: The Portuguese were the first to arrive in India (1498) during the period of the Delhi Sultanate/pre-Mughal era, and they established a presence that continued into the Mughal period before other European powers.
questions.subject: Modern India

questions.question_text: First railway line were laid down in India under which British Governor ?
questions.explanation: Lord Dalhousie is credited with introducing railways to India, with the first line opening during his tenure in 1853.
questions.subject: Modern India

questions.question_text: The Palk Strait separates India from which island nation?
questions.explanation: It connects the Bay of Bengal in the northeast with Palk Bay in the southwest.

questions.explanation: It connects the Bay of Bengal in the northeast with Palk Bay in the southwest.

questions.question_text: Gandhiji movement of boycotting the foreign goods aimed at-
questions.explanation: Boycotting foreign goods was intended to promote Swadeshi and revive Indian cottage industries like khadi spinning.
questions.subject: Modern India

questions.question_text: One who is present everywhere
questions.explanation: 'Omni' (all) + 'Present'.
questions.subject: English

questions.question_text: One who walks in sleep
questions.explanation: 'Somnus' (sleep) + 'Ambulare' (to walk).
questions.subject: English

questions.question_text: A government by a few people
questions.explanation: 'Oligos' means few.
questions.subject: English

questions.question_text: Select the correct indirect form: He said, 'The boy was playing in the rain.'
questions.option_a: He said that the boy had been playing in the rain.
questions.option_b: He said that the boy was playing in the rain.
questions.option_c: He said that the boy has been playing in the rain.
questions.option_d: He said that the boy is playing in the rain.
questions.explanation: Past Continuous ('was playing') changes to Past Perfect Continuous ('had been playing').
questions.subject: English

questions.question_text: Select the correct indirect form: He said, 'I shall go as soon as it is possible.'
questions.option_a: He said that he shall go as soon as it was possible.
questions.option_b: He said that he would go as soon as it was possible.
questions.option_c: He said that he would go as soon as it is possible.
questions.option_d: He said that he should go as soon as it was possible.
questions.explanation: 'Shall' changes to 'would' (for future intent) and 'is' changes to 'was' due to the past reporting verb.
questions.subject: English

questions.question_text: Select the correct direct form: He asked me if I had seen his brother.
questions.option_a: He said to me, 'Did you see my brother?'
questions.option_b: He said to me, 'Have you seen my brother?'
questions.option_c: He asked, 'Had you seen my brother?'
questions.option_d: He said to me, 'Did you saw my brother?'
questions.explanation: The Past Perfect 'had seen' in indirect speech reverts to Past Simple 'Did you see' in direct speech.
questions.subject: English

questions.question_text: It is time to water the plants.
questions.option_b: It is time when plants are watered.
questions.option_c: It is time the plants be watered.
questions.option_d: It is time for the plants to be watered.
questions.explanation: In such cases, the structure in passive is as follows: It is time + for + Object + to be + V3.
questions.subject: English

questions.question_text: Has he completed the assignments?
questions.option_a: Has the assignments being completed by him?
questions.option_b: Have the assignments been completed by him?
questions.option_c: Have the assignments completed by him?
questions.option_d: Has the assignments been completed by him?
questions.explanation: The structure is: Has/have + Subject + been + V3 + by + Object.
questions.subject: English

questions.question_text: Some people were helping the wounded woman.
questions.option_a: The wounded woman is being helped by some people.
questions.option_b: The wounded woman was being helped by some people.
questions.option_c: The wounded is helped by some people.
questions.option_d: The wounded woman was helped by some people.
questions.explanation: Subject + was/were + being + V3 + by + Object.
questions.subject: English

questions.question_text: Select the antonym of: BLEMISH
questions.explanation: Blemish is a small flaw; Perfection is the state of being free from all flaws.
questions.subject: English

questions.question_text: Select the antonym of: DEMISE
questions.explanation: Demise is a person's death; Birth is the emergence of a baby or other young from the body of its mother.
questions.subject: English

questions.question_text: Select the antonym of: CAPTIVATE
questions.explanation: Captivate means to attract; Repel means to drive away.
questions.subject: English

questions.question_text: The letter was written ____ red ink.
questions.explanation: 'In' is used for the medium (ink, pencil).
questions.subject: English

questions.question_text: He is senior ____ me.
questions.explanation: 'Senior' takes 'to'.
questions.subject: English

questions.question_text: A 'Good Samaritan' is...
questions.option_b: A person who helps others unselfishly
questions.explanation: Refers to a charitable or helpful person.
questions.subject: English

questions.question_text: Which personal characteristic is most crucial for a teacher when dealing with a classroom of students who have widely varying learning speeds and abilities?
questions.explanation: Patience is essential because learners progress at different rates; a teacher must be willing to explain concepts multiple times without frustration.
questions.subject: Teaching Aptitude
questions.topic: Role and Responsibilities of a Teacher

questions.question_text: What is the primary role of effective communication skills for a teacher in the classroom?
questions.option_a: To speak loudly enough to be heard in the hallway
questions.option_b: To use complex vocabulary to impress the school administration
questions.option_c: To translate complex concepts into clear, accessible ideas for students
questions.option_d: To win arguments against students who misbehave
questions.explanation: The core of teaching is transferring knowledge, which requires breaking down difficult topics into language that students can easily grasp.
questions.subject: Teaching Aptitude
questions.topic: Role and Responsibilities of a Teacher

questions.question_text: What role did spiritual development play in the ancient Indian education system?
questions.option_a: It was completely banned until the student reached old age
questions.option_b: It was reserved only for students studying to become priests
questions.option_c: It was inextricably intertwined with academic subjects to ensure holistic development
questions.option_d: It was considered a distraction from learning warfare and economics
questions.explanation: Unlike modern secular education, ancient traditions viewed spiritual growth as an essential foundation for all other types of learning.
questions.subject: Teaching Aptitude
questions.topic: Role and Responsibilities of a Teacher

questions.question_text: In the Guru-Shishya tradition, how was the curriculum typically structured?
questions.option_a: It was a rigid, standardized syllabus applied equally to everyone
questions.option_b: It was determined completely by the student's parents
questions.option_c: It was highly individualized based on the specific aptitude and capacity of each student
questions.option_d: It was decided by a central royal committee
questions.explanation: Gurus assessed the unique strengths and nature of each disciple and tailored their education accordingly, unlike modern standardized systems.
questions.subject: Teaching Aptitude
questions.topic: Role and Responsibilities of a Teacher

questions.question_text: A teacher overhears a highly sensitive, private conversation between two students regarding a medical issue. What does the ethical principle of confidentiality dictate?
questions.option_a: The teacher should immediately post the information on social media to seek advice
questions.option_b: The teacher must keep the information private unless it involves potential harm to the students or others
questions.option_c: The teacher should loudly confront the students in the middle of class
questions.option_d: The teacher must immediately tell the students' friends to offer support
questions.explanation: Confidentiality requires protecting student privacy; exceptions are strictly limited to situations where the student's safety is at immediate risk.
questions.subject: Teaching Aptitude
questions.topic: Role and Responsibilities of a Teacher

questions.question_text: Academic integrity for a teacher involves which of the following practices?
questions.option_a: Stealing lesson plans from colleagues and claiming them as original work
questions.option_b: Falsifying student attendance records to make the school look better
questions.option_c: Giving proper credit when using teaching materials or research created by other educators
questions.option_d: Helping students cheat on state exams to ensure high school rankings
questions.explanation: Just as students must not plagiarize, teachers are ethically bound to respect intellectual property and cite the sources of their materials.
questions.subject: Teaching Aptitude
questions.topic: Role and Responsibilities of a Teacher

questions.question_text: In a highly facilitated, student-centered classroom, who generally does the majority of the active talking, debating, and problem-solving?
questions.explanation: Facilitation shifts the cognitive load to the students; they learn by actively wrestling with the material, discussing it, and presenting solutions.
questions.subject: Teaching Aptitude
questions.topic: Role and Responsibilities of a Teacher

questions.question_text: How does a teacher acting explicitly as a 'co-learner' impact the traditional classroom hierarchy?
questions.option_a: It makes the teacher the absolute supreme ruler of the classroom
questions.option_b: It flattens the hierarchy, making the classroom a more collaborative and less authoritarian space
questions.option_c: It completely removes all rules and discipline from the school
questions.option_d: It forces the principal to take over teaching duties
questions.explanation: By learning alongside students, the teacher reduces the power distance, creating a safe space where students feel comfortable sharing ideas.
questions.subject: Teaching Aptitude
questions.topic: Role and Responsibilities of a Teacher

questions.question_text: What does the acronym NISHTHA stand for?
questions.option_a: National Institute for School Hardware and Technical Applications
questions.option_b: National Initiative for School Heads' and Teachers' Holistic Advancement
questions.option_c: New Information System for Higher Teaching and Academic Assessment
questions.option_d: Nodal Initiative for Student Health and Teacher Holistic Action
questions.explanation: NISHTHA stands for National Initiative for School Heads' and Teachers' Holistic Advancement.
questions.subject: Teaching Aptitude

questions.question_text: What type of educational platform is SWAYAM?
questions.option_b: A Massive Open Online Course (MOOC) platform
questions.option_c: A social media network for teenagers
questions.explanation: SWAYAM is an indigenous IT platform designed to host Massive Open Online Courses (MOOCs) providing high-quality education.
questions.subject: Teaching Aptitude

questions.question_text: What is the primary function of the PRASHAST app in schools?
questions.option_c: To screen students for the 21 disability conditions recognized under the RPwD Act 2016
questions.option_d: To track the GPS location of school buses
questions.explanation: The app is designed to help regular teachers and special educators screen children for suspected disabilities at the school level.
questions.subject: Teaching Aptitude

questions.question_text: What type of assistive technology would be most beneficial for a student with severe dyslexia who struggles with decoding text?
questions.explanation: Text-to-speech software reads digital text aloud, allowing students with dyslexia to access the content without struggling with decoding.
questions.subject: Teaching Aptitude

questions.question_text: In cyber ethics, what is 'phishing'?
questions.option_b: A fraudulent practice of sending emails purporting to be from reputable companies in order to induce individuals to reveal personal information
questions.option_d: A method of blocking inappropriate websites on school networks
questions.explanation: Phishing is a cyber attack that uses deceptive emails or messages to steal sensitive data like passwords or credit card numbers.
questions.subject: Teaching Aptitude

questions.question_text: What does 'LMS' stand for in the context of digital education?
questions.explanation: An LMS (like Moodle, Canvas, or Google Classroom) is a software application for the administration, documentation, tracking, reporting, and delivery of educational courses.
questions.subject: Teaching Aptitude

questions.question_text: What is a 'MOOC'?
questions.explanation: A MOOC is a free web-based distance learning program that is designed for the participation of large numbers of geographically dispersed students.
questions.subject: Teaching Aptitude

questions.question_text: The average of 10 numbers is 7. If each number is multiplied by 12, then the new average will be?
questions.explanation: When each observation is multiplied by a constant, the average is also multiplied by that constant. New average = 7 * 12 = 84.
questions.subject: Quant

questions.question_text: A student bought 4 books for Rs. 120 each, 6 books for Rs. 150 each, and 2 books for Rs. 90 each. What is the average price paid per book?
questions.subject: Quant

questions.question_text: The average of 5 consecutive numbers A, B, C, D, and E is 48. What is the product of A and E?
questions.explanation: The middle number C is 48. Therefore, the numbers are 46, 47, 48, 49, 50. A = 46 and E = 50. Their product is 46 * 50 = 2300.
questions.subject: Quant

questions.question_text: A train 100 m long is running at 36 km/hr. How much time will it take to pass a pole?
questions.explanation: Speed in m/s = 36 x 5/18 = 10. Time = Distance / Speed = 100 / 10 = 10 seconds.
questions.subject: Quant

questions.question_text: Sound travels at 330 m/s. If a thunder is heard 10 seconds after the flash of lightning, what is the distance to the storm?
questions.explanation: Distance = Speed x Time = 330 x 10 = 3300 m.
questions.subject: Quant

questions.question_text: If the 4th term of an AP is 14 and the 8th term is 30, find the first term.
questions.explanation: We have $a+3d=14$ and $a+7d=30$. Subtracting gives $4d=16$, so $d=4$. Substituting back, $a+12=14$, so $a=2$.
questions.subject: Quant

questions.question_text: The sum of the 4th and 8th terms of an AP is 24, and the sum of the 6th and 10th terms is 44. Find the first term.
questions.explanation: Equations: $2a+10d=24$ and $2a+14d=44$. Subtracting gives $4d=20$, $d=5$. Substituting yields $2a+50=24$, $2a=-26$, $a=-13$.
questions.subject: Quant

questions.question_text: Find the odd word out.
questions.explanation: Copper, Silver, and Gold are metals, whereas Wood is a non-metal organic material.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.question_text: Match the pair: Pen : Write :: Knife : ?
questions.explanation: A pen is primarily used as a tool to write, and a knife is primarily used as a tool to cut.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.question_text: If DAY is coded as FCa, then HOW is coded as?
questions.explanation: Each letter is shifted by $+2$. H(+2)=J, O(+2)=Q, W(+2)=Y.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.question_text: Find the missing number in the analogy. $11 : 121 :: 15 : ?$
questions.explanation: The relationship is $x : x^2$. The square of 11 is 121, and the square of 15 is 225.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.question_text: P is Q's sister. Q is a boy. R is P's mother. S is R's father. How is Q related to S?
questions.explanation: R is the mother of P and Q. S is the father of R, making S the grandfather of Q. Since Q is a boy, Q is the grandson.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.question_text: A man walks 10m North, turns right and walks 10m, then turns right again and walks 10m. In which direction is he from his starting point?
questions.explanation: He goes North, turns East, then turns South. The North and South distances cancel out, leaving him 10m East of the start.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.question_text: What is the angle between the hour and minute hands of a clock at 6:45?
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.question_text: In a certain code language, 'TRAIN' is written as '+-*/?' and 'SMART' is written as '%@*-+'. How will the word 'SAINT' be written in that code language?
questions.explanation: By directly mapping the letters to symbols: S is %, A is *, I is /, N is ?, T is +.
questions.subject: Reasoning
